**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include self-certificate failures in the exit gate**

Fresh evidence after `d90aa64` shows the new `reasons` gate still never reads `self_audit["all_pass"]`: when `--r1` contains a certificate that `verify()` rejects, the script prints `all_pass=False` but returns 0 if the corpus checks pass. This leaves one of the audit's advertised inputs able to fail without failing an automated reproduction, so append a reason for failed self-certificates (and preferably for an unexpectedly empty required set).

When `--file` is empty, or contains only malformed odd-length records such as `abc`, `total == passed == 0` and `decode_errors` remains empty because `decode()` returns `None`; the advertised full-database verifier therefore exits 0 after verifying no configurations. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Decode the extension alphabet by its declared ordering**

When decoding post-February-2026 configurations with columns above 61, `ord(c) + 1` does not implement the archived 90-character alphabet: for example `#` should map to 62 but maps to 36, colliding with `a`; additionally, the later `"@" in line` check rejects `@` even though it is now an alphabet symbol. Thus the decoder cannot reproduce the n>61 records targeted by the next round; use the published alphabet string as an index map while handling legacy records separately.

When the initial 300-second scan stops partway through n=54, this follow-up decodes but never mathematically verifies any record below 55. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the frozen B3 energy bound**

The cycle-1 acceptance contract in `round.json` fixes B3 at no more than twice the Stage A maximum, but this applies a `1e-10` floor; with the committed Stage A residuals around `1e-14`, that relaxes the limit by roughly three orders of magnitude and can report an energy pass that the admitted rule rejects. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare matching physical lag windows across N**

For the implemented field `cos(2πkj/N)`, a lag index `r` represents the normalized separation `r/N`; reusing the same integer `WINDOWS` for `N=2048` and `N=4096` therefore halves every physical fitting interval. Consequently, the reported `m4096 - m2048` values conflate resolution sensitivity with a factor-of-two window shift and cannot support the claimed N-sensitivity analysis. Scale the lag indices with N (or otherwise hold the physical interval fixed) before comparing the slopes.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply both cutoffs in the companion audit**

Fresh evidence after `e3c93de` is that the companion audit still applies the marginal formula without its UV condition and says the `>1.9` regime is unreachable merely because `r < 0.0248` lies below the lattice spacing. For this band, that range has `k_hi·r ≪ 1`, so the marginal formula is invalid and the exact exponent instead exceeds 1.9 at integer lags 1 and 2 because of the analytic `r²` regime; meanwhile the actual marginal window is `[15,21]` with exponent ≈1.72. This leaves the two canonical reports with contradictory cutoff interpretations, so this paragraph needs the same UV/IR correction as `CANONICAL_FACTS.md`.

The amplitude guard discards the amplitudes returned by `make_field` and compares the field against `[1.0]`, so its analytic reference energy is unrelated to `u_ref`. In fact, the unmodified `u_ref` already yields a relative residual of about 0.208 against `[1.0]`, above the 0.10 threshold, meaning this check reports success even without the 1.5× corruption and therefore does not validate that amplitude inflation is detected.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid treating phase-only seeds as statistical uncertainty**

For this full-period sum of integer Fourier modes, the periodic full-domain `S2` calculation cancels cross terms, making the quadratic structure function independent of the randomly seeded phases. The five slopes are consequently identical up to roundoff, so this computed `sf_std` cannot measure seed-to-seed statistical error or support the frozen uncertainty criterion; use genuinely independent sampled realizations/subwindows or classify this as an analytic/numerical check instead.

On a clean checkout or in CI, the sibling research repositories are normally absent, so this branch prints `SKIP` for every external locator and still exits successfully.
